item.title: Europe’s Outrage Over Maduro Arrest Reflects Poor Understanding of Oil Industry
item.description: The dramatic arrest of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro sent shock waves around the world. Yet nowhere was the reaction more negative – and more baffling – than in the European Union, where outrage swept through public discourse, a stark contrast to the generally positive reaction in the U.S. and elsewhere.

item.title: A speculation on military risk with offshore wind — AI submarines
item.description: It is up to the Trump administration to carefully assess the threat of tiny AI subs hiding among the massive steel monopiles of offshore wind facilities. Results might range from banning facilities in certain areas to developing detection and defense systems where development is allowed, if that happens. In some cases, the monopiles are already there. Perhaps they should be removed.

item.title: The Problem with ‘Peer Review’
item.description: The truth of ‘peer review’ was that it was the means by which bureaucratic controls were imposed, indeed, self-imposed, on intellectual activity. That is it.

item.title: Southeast Asia Continues Hurtling Down the Net Zero Suicide Track
item.description: Net Zero by 2050 may exist in models. It is not tenable in the real world. And policy built on that confusion risks condemning Southeast Asia to slower growth, higher costs and diminished prospects — all in service of a creed whose high priests are already losing the faith.
